chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym and ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from one who heard it, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, concerning:

If a woman becomes pure from menstruation but has not touched water, then her husband should not have intercourse with her until she performs ghusl. If he does so, then there is no harm in it. And he said: her touching water is more beloved to me.

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: more beloved or preferable to me
key_terms.تَمَسَّ الْمَاءَ: to touch water, meaning to wash or begin ritual purification
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Can a husband have intercourse with his wife after menstruation ends but before she performs ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on intercourse with a woman after her menstrual bleeding has ceased but before she has performed ghusl. It indicates a preference for waiting until she washes, while also stating that if intercourse occurs before ghusl, there is no harm in it.
